channel.title: Round Table China
channel.description: Round Table is a premier English radio/podcast show, straight from Beijing. Hear what's buzzing on the Internet and the main streets, see the latest lifestyle trends, and feel the pulse of life in China, Round Table is your golden ticket. With dynamic cultural exchanges between hosts from diverse backgrounds, we take you on a journey deep into modern China. We invite you to join our conversation! Shoot us an email or a voice memo at roundtablepodcast@qq.com. Let the fun begin!
channel.itunes:author: China Plus

item.title: Inside China's inland waterway travel boom
item.description: Forget the whirlwind tour. Travelers are swapping packed itineraries for China's inland waterways, where cozy cabins, great food, and cultural stops along the Yangtze and Pearl Rivers turn the journey into a getaway in itself. What is behind the appeal of slow river travel, and how is it reshaping the way people experience China? On the show: Steve, Fei Fei & Yushun

item.title: New study links postpartum depression, breast milk
item.description: New research from Nanjing University has uncovered a surprising possible link between postpartum depression, breast milk and a baby's developing brain. But the science is only part of the story. From breastfeeding pressure and maternal guilt to traditional Chinese confinement practices and postnatal care, the support new mothers receive can make all the difference. On the show: Steve, Fei Fei & Yushun

item.title: The Soapbox: Nanjing's free noodle dilemma
item.description: Imagine watching your paying customers vanish because a neighbor started giving the exact same thing away for free. A viral charity controversy in China poses a real-life ethical puzzle: when pure generosity threatens the livelihoods of everyone else on the block, where does helping a crowd cross into harming a community? On the show: Steve, Yushan & Yushun

item.title: Smarter heating for a colder winter
item.description: Winter is bearing down on China. Between surging seasonal energy demand, aging urban pipelines, and remote communities sitting far off the grid, the race is on to warm hundreds of millions of homes without warming the planet. What does it really take to make winter heating safer, smarter, and more sustainable across a nation of 1.4 billion people? On the show: Steve, Yushan & Yushun

item.title: Young renters, elderly roommates
item.description: What if your next roommate was 80 years old? Across China, nursing homes are opening their doors to young people, offering affordable accommodation in exchange for companionship and volunteer services. But what makes this arrangement attractive to both generations, and can it become a sustainable model of housing and elderly care? On the show: Steve, Yushan & Yushun

item.title: Why can't we fix anything?
item.description: A leaking tap. A wobbly toilet seat. Flat-pack furniture with confusing instructions. For many young adults, these count as genuine emergencies, and they're signing up for classes and scouring online tutorials to solve them. What does this boom in basic-skills learning say about growing up today? On the show: Steve, Yushan & Yushun

item.title: APEC, tech tours, and the new China Haul
item.description: Empty suitcases are meeting autonomous rides and drone-delivered lunches in Shenzhen, where sightseeing now doubles as a hands-on hardware scout. As APEC draws global founders and dealmakers to China's innovation capital, international visitors are moving past souvenir shopping to test prototypes, tour bustling electronics hubs, and strike deals directly on the ground. On the show: Steve, Yushan & Yushun

item.title: Turning trash into cash after dark
item.description: Across China's big cities, a gritty, old-school chore has become Gen Z's favorite late-night ritual. After dark, young residents head downstairs to feed cardboard boxes and plastic bottles into automated recycling kiosks for pocket change. Is this micro-earning habit just about tighter budgets, or does it reflect a change in how young consumers think about trash? On the show: Steve, Yushan & Yushun

item.title: The unexpected keys to college success
item.description: A study of nearly 80,000 undergraduates reveals that the things students often try to escape, like stress and responsibility, might actually be the key to a better college experience. The findings challenge common assumptions about university life and offer new insights into how young people in China and around the world build connections and shape their futures.On the show: Steve, Yushan & Yangyang

item.title: APEC spotlight: the future of smart manufacturing
item.description:
Ahead of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, the future of manufacturing is firmly on the agenda. Round Table's Fei Fei traveled to Foshan, a major manufacturing hub in the Greater Bay Area, to see what industrial transformation looks like on the factory floor. There, she spoke with Samson Chen with a leading heavy machinery manufacturer, about how the region's industries are innovating, improving efficiency, and staying connected to international markets. On the show: Steve, Fei Fei & Yushun
Check out the interview in video: news.cgtn.com

item.title: COP31: can global trade spare the ocean?
item.description: With the global climate spotlight back on at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, can the ocean be a true partner in the climate fight? Picture a coastal city chasing a roaring economy, a packed international port, and a pristine shoreline all at once. Can those ambitions coexist, or does trade inevitably leave a scar on nature? On the show: Steve, Fei Fei & Yushun

item.title: APEC spotlights Shenzhen's green push
item.description:
Shenzhen is known around the world for technology and innovation. But as the host city of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in 2026, it's also spotlighting another side of its development: its push to become greener. Round Table's Yushun recently traveled to Shenzhen to see these efforts firsthand. He brings back a closer look at what other Asia-Pacific cities might learn from its experience. On the show: Steve, Fei Fei & Yushun

Check out Yushun's video: news.cgtn.com

item.title: The Soapbox: police station parenting
item.description: Would you take your child to a police station for refusing to do homework? In China, some parents have. In at least one case, a boy who'd dodged his assignment all day finished it in an hour once he got there. Some call it a clever fix. Others see a line between discipline and intimidation. On the show: Steve, Fei Fei & Yushun

item.title: What skills will matter in the age of AI?
item.description: As AI takes on more tasks once handled by humans, from writing and analysis to creativity and decision-making, what will set people apart in the workplace? For young people entering an AI-driven job market, the challenge is not simply learning to use new technology but understanding where human skills will matter most. Singapore-based entrepreneur Ian Chew discusses the skills, mindset, and qualities the next generation will need to stay relevant with Fei Fei and Yushan.

item.title: Qigong: the barely-working-out secret
item.description: The secret to a better morning might not be working out harder, but barely working out at all. Qigong, an ancient Chinese practice of slow, breath-led movement, is quietly replacing high-intensity routines across the West. Can clinical evidence cut through the wellness buzz, and can 10 mindful minutes really change your body and mind? On the show: Steve, Fei Fei & Yushan

item.title: Beijing's school meal overhaul
item.description: Beijing is banning outsourced school lunches, and by 2027 every school in the city must run its own canteen, with food buying centralized at the district level. What difference will it make for students, parents, and schools, and does bringing cooking back in-house actually make meals safer and better? On the show: Steve, Fei Fei & Yushan

item.title: Are you low on vitamin D?
item.description: Think fatigue, muscle weakness and constant achiness are just part of modern life? New research points to a hidden culprit most of us never check: vitamin D. Adults in China are overwhelmingly falling short, with younger people hit hardest by indoor lifestyles. / Is your prefrontal cortex attractive (17:42)? On the show: Steve, Fei Fei & Yushun

item.title: Double Eleven goes AI
item.description: China's biggest online sales festival is in full swing, and the standout helper this year is artificial intelligence. AI is lending a hand at every turn, from shoppers weighing their options to courier firms bracing for a parcel avalanche, and it's even flying off the shelves itself. On the show: Steve, Fei Fei & Yushun

item.title: The Soapbox: should the subway charge you for lingering?
item.description: A time restriction in Guangzhou is catching subway riders off guard and sparking debate about extra fees for staying underground too long. The policy raises questions about whether public transit systems should charge passengers for the time they spend inside their stations. On the show: Steve, Yushan & Yushun
